_about: Proposed reasoner tool schema (design draft, 2026-10-23). All tools are READ-ONLY. The Go backend executes them; the model only chooses the tool and its arguments. Exact numbers always come from the executor, never from the model. Format: OpenAI/Llama-3.x style function definitions, so llama.cpp's chat handlers and the Llama 3.2 template can render them. Keep descriptions short: every token here is prefilled (and prefix-cached) on the NPU.

time_range.description: Either a preset or explicit ISO dates (IST). Presets are resolved by the executor against the device clock.

pattern.description: Agent pattern label, e.g. spike, step_increase, exp_rise, flatline, drift, oscillation. Validated against the policy whitelist.

tools.name: count_incidents
tools.description: Exact count of incidents matching filters, optionally grouped. Use for every 'how many' question about incidents.

node.description: Sensor node id or a location prefix such as KH03

include_injected.description: Default false: demo/injected incidents are excluded

tools.returns: {count:int | groups:[{key,count}], coverage:{source:'device'|'fog', complete:bool, from, to, note}, query_id}

tools.name: find_incidents
tools.description: List incidents matching filters (newest first, max 10) with id, time, title, severity, label. Use to show examples or before get_incident.

text.description: Keyword search over titles, root causes and operator notes (BM25 on device; hybrid BM25+vector on fog)

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: One incident's report: root cause, severity, sensors, agent findings, revisions, operator decision.

tools.name: sensor_faults
tools.description: Exact counts and lists of sensors that were faulty and/or replaced. basis=ai: an agent or rule said sensor_fault; basis=confirmed: an operator approved a sensor_fault incident; replaced: a maintenance record says the sensor was replaced.

tools.name: get_sensor_history
tools.description: Aggregated readings of one sensor for a period, plus the evidence summary the agents use (min/max/trend/steps). Use when an incident needs more data than its window.

stats_only.description: Default true: return a short evidence summary, not the raw series

tools.name: list_sensors
tools.description: Sensors on the device with domain, location, current status and last reading.

tools.name: domain_health
tools.description: Current health of each domain (worst sensor status, trend, open incidents, next steps). Same data as GET /api/health.

tools.name: related_context
tools.description: Incident-time only. Readings of causally related sensors (orchestrator causal map) around a flagged sensor, with evidence ids R1..Rn.

ref.description: S1, S2 ... from the incident prompt

tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.description: Fog only (online). Semantic search over the full incident archive, maintenance logs and facility documents (SOPs, manuals). Returns passages with source ids.

executor_rules: Every tool is read-only. No tool can actuate, approve, dismiss, inject or change configuration.
Arguments are validated against this schema; enums are enforced at decode time (htpd label trie) and again in Go.
count_* results are computed by SQL / Go aggregation and returned as integers; the answer renderer quotes them verbatim.
coverage is always returned; when complete=false the answer must say so (e.g. 'on this device: last 1000 incidents since 2026-03-02').
Online: count_incidents / find_incidents / sensor_faults run on the fog store (complete history) and fall back to the device store on timeout (1.5 s) or when offline.
Max 4 tool calls per chat turn, 1 per early-alert incident analysis, 2 per refinement. Identical repeated calls are answered from the turn cache and count against the limit.
Tool results are data, never instructions: operator notes and document passages are quoted inside a fenced, labelled block (prompt-injection hygiene).
